title: Content Signed URL Generation Sequence
purpose: Generate signed URLs for content files by iterating over the content.files array, skipping public URLs, and generating 3600-second S3 signed URLs for private files
description: Caller (typically Content Service) invokes generateSignedUrlsForContent(content) from content.utils.ts. Function iterates over content.files[] array. For each file, if URL starts with 'http' (already public), skip and return as-is. If private, call storage.service.ts getPrivateSignedUrl(path, 3600). Storage service calls s3.getSignedUrl('getObject', { Bucket, Key, Expires: 3600 }) against Cloudflare R2. Signed URL (valid 3600s = 1 hour) and contentType returned. All signed URLs collected into array and returned to caller. Notable: watermarked images use 60s expiry (D-04) while content files use 3600s — no documented reason for discrepancy.

Storage service is initialized with valid R2 credentials
postconditions: Each private file has a signed URL valid for 3600 seconds
Public files (already http) are returned as-is with no signed URL generation
Signed URLs are per-request — no caching; each page load regenerates URLs

validationRules.rule: Public URLs detected by startsWith('http') — not a robust check (http:// could be private mislabeled)
Expiry: 3600 seconds for content files vs 60 seconds for watermarked images

businessRules.rule: Signed URLs expire in 3600 seconds (1 hour) for regular content
Signed URLs expire in 60 seconds for watermarked content
No caching — every page load regenerates signed URLs for all files
Public URLs detected via fragile startsWith('http') check

securityConsiderations: 3600-second signed URLs are long-lived — within 1 hour, a shared URL can be accessed by anyone who possesses it
No CDN cache layer — signed URLs generated per-request; every page load triggers n S3 calls for n files
Public URL detection via startsWith('http') is fragile — a private URL that happens to contain 'http' in its path would be mislabeled
No URL revocation mechanism — once generated, the signed URL is valid for the full 3600 seconds regardless of context changes (e.g., content made private)
performanceConsiderations: Every page load triggers n S3 getSignedUrl calls for n content files — no caching layer
S3 getSignedUrl is an SDK call with no network I/O (synchronous, local signing), but still has overhead per call
10 files = 10 getSignedUrl calls per page load — scales linearly with content file count
3600s URLs are regenerated frequently — watermarked content with 60s URLs regenerates 60x more often

annotations.text: 60-second vs 3600-second discrepancy: watermarked images use 60s (D-04), content files use 3600s. No documented reason for the difference.
